purpose: The published default town positions (release 3: production catchment tiling with an exp(-D/800 km) heartland prior on score and catchment density, count held at the natural production count) have only been checked on the Han and Roman pools they were developed on. Vidarbha is the one regional survey outside those pools. This scores the published rule there with the original frozen metrics.
status_of_source: Exposed and declared spent for parameter tuning on 2026-11-11 after the adaptive L450 candidate failed against the fixed L800 control. This is therefore an exposed-region transfer check, not a blind test. No parameter of the release-3 rule is changed, and no new candidate will be chosen from these scores.
known_before_declaration: Archived 3 km EH-S central results (rebuilt-input runs not yet computed): production 10 km capture by zone 0.238 / 0.063 / 0.063; fixed L800 0.000 / 0.063 / 0.438; equal-zone mean percentile: fixed L800 0.461, lead L450 0.470. The release-3 rule has never been run on Vidarbha. The survey files were re-downloaded and match their recorded hashes exactly.
inputs: Rebuilt with the original prepare_inputs code on the rebuilt global harvest grid (output/land_people/earth/earth.npz, rebuilt 2026-11-13 from public sources; not byte-identical to the lost original). Every alternative, old and new, is rerun on the same rebuilt inputs; the archived results are reported beside them to show input drift.
alternatives: production_seed1 (legacy allocator), release3_L800 (published default rule, deterministic), and as drift controls fixed_L800_seed1 and lead_L450 seeds 1,7,19,43,97 exactly as before.
metrics: Original frozen definitions: primary 3 km grid, EH-S 'yes' cohort, central coordinates, three 13 km frames with equal weight; 10 km known-site capture and mean within-frame opportunity percentile. The release-3 opportunity field is score x exp(-D/800), which ranks cells exactly as the archived fixed L800 field; production's is the environmental score. Secondary 9 km grid, other cohorts and the eight coordinate offsets reported, never used to choose.
guard: The release-3 rule is compared with production, which it replaced. Same support requirement as before (at least 30 distinct cell-zone units, at least 2 zones with at least 8). Non-inferiority, the original margins: capture(release3) - capture(production) >= -0.10 and percentile(release3) - percentile(production) >= -0.05, and every count, eligibility, uniqueness and spacing constraint passes.
consequence: Pass: the published rule is not worse than the legacy allocator on the one external survey. Fail: reported plainly beside the release-3 report; the default is not changed automatically.
review: Independent recomputation of percentiles and captures from the stored placements and matches; placement constraints; fresh byte replay of numeric files.
